Hospital Admission History and Physical
Date: 09/22/2026
Patient: Valery Erdman, 88-year-old female

Chief Complaint:
Admitted 09/22/2026 for intractable back pain, NRS 8/10 despite IV analgesia.

History of Present Illness:
Ms. Erdman presents with severe back pain that has necessitated hospital admission. The pain is described as intense and unrelieved by intravenous analgesics.

Past Medical History:
Includes hypertension and osteoarthritis.

Physical Examination:
Vital signs are stable. On examination, tenderness is noted over the lumbar spine. Neurological exam reveals no focal deficits.

Assessment:
Intractable back pain requiring inpatient management.

Plan:
Continue pain management with close monitoring. Further diagnostic evaluation will be considered to determine underlying cause. Consultations with pain management and orthopedics will be arranged as needed.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/16/2026
Patient: Valery Erdman, 88-year-old female

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/16/2026: acute osteoporotic T11 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

No other acute abnormalities are identified in the thoracic or lumbar spine.

Impression:
Acute osteoporotic compression fracture at T11 with associated bone marrow edema on STIR sequences, consistent with recent injury.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Further management should be determined by the referring physician based on the clinical scenario.

Spine Intervention Consultation

History:
Valery Erdman presents for evaluation of back pain associated with a known vertebral fracture.

Examination:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Assessment:

Plan:

Further interventional options will be considered based on bone density results and clinical follow-up.
